text:
Avery Johnson: anyone have (or can we get) a “backup demo” recording? Had 2 calls this week where Console metrics were empty at the start and I had to hand-wave. Would love a clean video we can play if something flakes.

Soojin Lee: yep, we’ve been working on this. We have a draft Loom from last week (rough cut) but we need SE narration notes so the story matches the new talk track.

Camila Reyes: +1. The video is solid visually but the voiceover is too “marketing-y” right now. We want it to sound like Markus / SE style.

Hannah Schmitt: would be huge for exec demos too. Even if we don’t play it, having 30–60s clips for “fallback routing” and “cost breakdown” would help.

Markus Klein: we should do it. Quick Q: are you looking for a single 20–25 min end-to-end recording, or modular clips we can stitch (core API / economics / reliability / observability)?

Soojin Lee: ideally modular.
- Clip 1 (3–4 min): “hello world” chat + streaming
- Clip 2 (3–5 min): structured output + tool calling (show JSON + tool result)
- Clip 3 (3–4 min): production economics (batching/caching toggle → token cost / latency change)
- Clip 4 (2–3 min): reliability (fallback routing / graceful degradation narrative)
- Clip 5 (4–5 min): Console tour (cost, latency, errors, rollouts)
Plus a stitched “standard 25-min demo” version.

Camila Reyes: and we need a 12–15 min “exec cut” that hits: why Redwood, 1 live flow, 1 Console view, 1 enterprise/security slide (narrative only). No deep clicks.

Markus Klein: ok. For SE narration notes, do you want: exact script, or bullet beats + callouts?

Soojin Lee: bullet beats is fine as long as we get:
- the “why this matters” line per segment
- where to pause for questions
- what not to say (avoid over-claiming Dedicated in a hosted demo tenant)

Renee Sullivan: I can provide the beats for tool calling + structured output (we have the scripted scenario runner). Also can provide the “expected output” lines so it doesn’t feel improvised.

Alex Martinez: for the SDK snippets in the recording: please pin to the demo-safe versions and avoid showing local env vars on screen. If you show code, keep it to the minimal calls + `stream=True` example.

Elliot Price: where do we want to host final assets? Confluence page + Drive folder? Also need a quick note in the runbook: “If live demo fails → play clip X”.

Camila Reyes: Drive for the video files + a Confluence hub page linking:
- “exec cut”
- “full demo stitched”
- individual clips
- deck slide numbers that match each clip

Avery Johnson: also important: can we make sure the recording doesn’t show internal-only URLs / tenant IDs / anything that looks scary? Prospect paranoia is real.

Markus Klein: yep. We’ll record in the demo org but we’ll use sanitized naming. Suggest:
Org: “Redwood Demo Org”
Project: “Synth Support Agent”
Routes: “chat-prod-econ”, “chat-reliability”, “embeddings-search”
No customer logos.

Soojin Lee: perfect. Also please avoid showing raw audit logs in the video unless we’re doing the security module. We got feedback that it spooks people.

Hannah Schmitt: +1. If we mention audit logs, keep it as “available in Enterprise” with a screenshot in deck.

Markus Klein: proposed plan:
1) Camila shares the current Loom draft + timestamps
2) SE team adds narration notes directly as comments (time-coded)
3) We re-record voiceover + re-cut into modules
4) Elliot publishes hub page + “backup mode” instructions

Camila Reyes: works. I’ll DM the draft link and the edit doc.

Renee Sullivan: I’ll add narration beats for the tool calling moment. Key line we should hit: “This is the same API surface across hosted, Dedicated, and Private — what changes is the policy + capacity isolation.”

Alex Martinez: and for the structured output: emphasize “schema validation / retries” not “prompt magic”. Show the JSON schema briefly, then the model output.

Elliot Price: timeline? We have training sessions next week.

Soojin Lee: aiming for v1 by EOW if we can. Even if it’s not perfect, having something is better than scrambling mid-demo.

Markus Klein: I can do narration notes today + re-record tomorrow morning. If we need extra hands for the Console segments, I’ll pull in Dylan/Chloe but I think we can keep it lightweight.

Avery Johnson: thank you. If you can include a 20–30s clip where Console shows token-level breakdown (cost + latency) that’s the one I’ll use the most.

Camila Reyes: noted. Also: do we want captions baked in? A lot of prospects watch recordings on mute.

Markus Klein: yes, captions. And we should trim any waiting/loading time. No one needs to watch spinners.

Soojin Lee: :thumbsup: please send narration notes by ~3pm PT if possible.

Markus Klein: will do.

Elliot Price: once final is ready, I’ll add a one-liner to the demo checklist: “preload the exec cut in a browser tab as contingency.”

Hannah Schmitt: love it. This will save us.

Camila Reyes: dropping this here so it doesn’t get lost: please say “synthetic workload” at least once during the Console tour. We want to be explicit it’s not customer data.

Markus Klein: good call. I’ll include that in the intro to Console.

Soojin Lee: awesome. Thanks all — will share draft shortly.
